item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-ba956ef329c89fab","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"ARTICLE 19 reported that Mexico's security conditions for its staff deteriorated despite state protection measures: staff were followed, homes watched, its director was assaulted, and its website suffered a malware-disrupting attack. It attributed the wider context to continuing violence, corruption, impunity, and coercive restrictions on expression, association, and assembly.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.6","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Background evidence from 2013-2014; not specific to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The document concerns Mexico but predates López Obrador's presidency; it does not attribute these events to him.","limitations":["Historical context only; no 2023 outcome or direct AMLO responsibility is established."]},{"source_id":"SRC-325aa42f88ad68a3","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"RSF reported that López Obrador and officials used combative, stigmatizing rhetoric against journalists, including a weekly 'Who's Who in Fake News' segment, while constitutional press protections remained formally in place. It also reported concentrated media ownership, collusion between officials and organized crime, lethal threats and killings of journalists, and that the president had not carried out reforms needed to reduce violence and impunity.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","4B.10","7B.1","7B.2"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published as Mexico 2022 evidence; relevant as recent pre-2023 context.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributes official rhetoric and failure to carry out reforms to López Obrador and his government.","limitations":["The page is a 2022 country profile, not a contemporaneous 2023 assessment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-973a6b3821bd289c","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"López Obrador made the electricity reform a near-personal political and policy priority, seeking to strengthen the state electricity company CFE and reorient the energy market. The constitutional initiative failed because Morena lacked the two-thirds congressional majority, while a related electricity law was upheld by the Supreme Court after litigation.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","5B.1","5B.4","5B.6","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2022 evidence, relevant to the program and institutional constraints entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributes the initiative, political pressure, and policy objective to López Obrador.","limitations":["Does not establish 2023 implementation or economic outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c15ddc65df8099fa","start_unit":5,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"Centro Prodh states that the Ayotzinapa disappearances involved 43 students, six executions, torture indicators, and many injured victims, and that authorities' obstruction prevented full truth, investigation, prosecution, and sanctioning. In 2023 it reported that families denounced obstruction before the IACHR, criticized official disqualifications and protection of the Army, and noted an unusual change in the precautionary measure of an implicated general.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.4","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The core abuses occurred in 2014; units 10-11 provide direct 2023 developments.","ruler_attribution":"The 2023 criticism concerns the federal government's handling under López Obrador, including alleged Army protection and obstruction; the source is an advocacy organization.","limitations":["The source presents an affected-families and human-rights-organization perspective; precise attribution for each obstructive act is not specified."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f14fcb1c8ad38d4a","start_unit":4,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"HRW reported that serious human-rights violations and impunity continued under López Obrador; he expanded military roles in law enforcement, immigration, customs, social programs, and mega-projects. It described weak investigations, torture, disappearances, attacks on journalists and defenders, inadequate protection funding, abusive migrant expulsions and detention practices, gaps in disability and women's rights, inadequate COVID response, fossil-fuel policies, and limited climate ambition. It also recorded favorable institutional actions, including greater disappearance-data transparency, recognition of the UN disappearances committee's jurisdiction, and participation in international human-rights and migration initiatives.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.7","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.6","6B.8","6B.9","6B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Events of 2020-2021; useful background but not a 2023-specific report.","ruler_attribution":"The report directly attributes the military expansion and several policy choices to López Obrador's administration.","limitations":["The source predates 2023 and combines national conditions with policies whose later status is not shown."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1eef832b1b98f0c1","start_unit":3,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"EL PAÍS describes López Obrador as a highly popular, charismatic leader whose Morena movement controlled major power levers. It reports achievements including higher minimum wages, stronger social programs, and a historical poverty reduction, alongside expanded military power, lack of progressive tax reform, increased wealth among the richest, personal intervention in Morena's succession, favorable treatment of Sheinbaum, and efforts to recruit opposition governors. It also reports his combative use of public rhetoric, tendency to blame predecessors, and defense of longtime ally Ignacio Ovalle despite the Segalmex corruption scandal.","question_ids":["3B.3","4B.2","4B.3","4B.5","4B.8","4B.10","5B.1","5B.5","5B.8","5B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.7","6B.9","6B.10","7B.2","7B.5","7B.9","7B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Retrospective article published after the 2023 period;
